This is a controlled CUDA float64 port of the spherical finite-volume solver,
not a separate physical model. The original CPU source and executable remain
unchanged. Build with `make` in this directory, then run
`./mhd_cuda --config /absolute/path/run.cfg`. CUDA 12 and an sm_89 GPU are the
current tested build targets; override NVCCFLAGS for another architecture.

The key/value configuration and outputs follow `../README.md`. Additional
configuration is `flux_variant=global_llf` (original global GLM-speed Rusanov)
or `flux_variant=split_llf` (exact normal-B/q GLM interface preprocessing,
local fast-magnetosonic Rusanov for the remaining MHD variables). These select
the same two controlled CPU reference variants in `../induction_cpu/`.
Neither choice represents a constrained-transport algorithm.

All evolution arithmetic, conserved states, reconstructed primitives, geometry,
and boundary interpolation use double precision. Fused multiply-add is disabled
to make the CPU comparison strict. Geometry, initial conditions, angular basis
vectors, and configuration are computed by a frozen host copy of the CPU
reference. Conserved states, fluxes, RK stages, and boundary maps then remain on
the GPU. Only reduced scalar diagnostics, requested probes, and snapshots cross
the device boundary. Snapshot output retains the CPU float32 NumPy format;
probe output retains its 12-digit CSV precision.

The optional boundary CSV columns `emf_theta_nT_AU_day` and
`emf_phi_nT_AU_day` are angularly interpolated and taken from the left time
interval. Their value is zero before the first map and at or after the final
map. Other primitive map quantities retain linear interpolation in time.
The boundary adds Btheta=-Ephi/vr and Bphi=Etheta/vr to the rotating Parker
field, with the same r0/r initialization scaling as the controlled CPU source.
This center-sampled electric-field interpolation is an approximation to the
external discrete surface closure; it does not impose that staggered closure
exactly on this finite-volume mesh.

`outer_magnetic_radial_scaling=1` extrapolates Br proportional to r^-2 and
tangential B proportional to r^-1 in the outer ghost layers. Its default is
zero. The density, pressure, velocity, and cleaning variable are copied there,
matching the controlled CPU reference.

The SSPRK2, GLM energy/damping, strict positivity checks, global first-order
fallback and timestep-halving logic follow the CPU reference. There are no
positivity floors. Statistics report rejected attempts and fallback steps.
Each directional flux, update, reduction, and ghost operation uses a separate
kernel. The program does not request exclusive GPU mode or change device power
settings. Only one instance should run at a time under the shared GPU runner.

All device allocations are tracked and hard-capped at 2.3 GB, leaving roughly
200 MB within the 2.5 GB agreed budget for runtime/context overhead. A preflight
check requires another 500 MB free beyond the estimated arrays. Host allocation
omits all CPU stepping work arrays: it keeps only initial/output u and p plus
geometry, approximately 248 bytes per ghost-extended cell. The runner should
monitor resident host and device memory and enforce its wall-time budget;
RLIMIT_AS is unsuitable for CUDA's large virtual address reservation.
The frozen host preflight still estimates the more conservative FP64 working
storage even for the FP32 executable. Balanced192×64×192 passes and has been
benchmarked; a256×80×256 FP32 case would require a separately reviewed host
preflight change despite fitting the actual device data cap.

`python validate.py` executes controlled CPU/CUDA tests, writes isolated inputs
and results under `validation/`, and compares final fields and probe outputs.
`reference_provenance.json` pins the source and header hashes.
`freeze_host_reference.py` regenerates that header only when explicitly invoked
after source review; `make` never silently refreshes it. Regeneration requires
repeating the CPU/CUDA agreement checks before production refinement.

The separate `mhd_cuda_fp32` target uses float for every high-volume device
state, normal/area/volume/basis, reconstruction, flux, gravity, RK update,
cleaning, and reduction. Host time and geometry construction, boundary coordinate
axes and phase lookup remain double. The map values are float. Snapshots and
probes are converted back to the same host output format; this does not restore
lost device precision. `build_fp32.py` generates the separate sources with
explicit float constants and sqrtf/powf/fabsf/copysignf, and records the frozen
parent and generated hashes. It is an explicit regeneration step, not a make
dependency. `validate_fp32.py` compares saved FP64 runs with FP32 reruns,
including PN-only incident flux, fallback counts, and divergence diagnostics.
Precision agreement is a separate requirement from spatial or flux-scheme
convergence.

`kernel_benchmark_fp32 config.cfg` and its FP64 equivalent initialize the same
problem, then time five calls to each directional flux kernel with CUDA events.
They do not evolve the wind. These are separate executables so profiling never
modifies a production solver. Shared GPU activity can increase measured time;
the result is useful as an upper bound for short-kernel coordination.

The separate `mhd_cuda_fp32_cme` target adds the optional `cme_boundary_csv`
control. `build_cme_fp32.py` reuses the exact controlled CPU ConeBoundary class
for host parsing and initialization, then adds its matching device boundary
envelope. Times, inertial cone axes, angular separation and envelope weights
are computed in double; only the resulting n/v/T primitive changes are float.
The largest space/time envelope wins overlapping cones, with later rows winning
ties. Br and the optional electric corrections remain unchanged; the Parker
tangential field uses the changed radial speed. This is a conditional plasma
cone, without magnetic flux-rope structure. `validate_cme_fp32.py` checks exact
identity when no cone table is present, a synthetic overlapping-cone CPU check,
and a full25day coarse control against the controlled CPU executable.

`mhd_cuda_fp32_async_hlle` is a separate third flux control. It requires
`flux_variant=split_hlle` and retains optional interval E, outer B scaling and
cones. Exact GLM interface preprocessing is followed by Davis local fast-wave
bounds and the two-wave HLL flux. When all MHD waves travel outward/inward,
the physical left/right flux is selected. The explicit normal-B/q flux correction
is retained. This changes numerical transport and must be compared as a method,
separately from FP32 or execution-order checks. `build_hlle.py` generates its
matching controlled CPU reference under `hlle_cpu/`; `validate_hlle.py` compares
tiny and complete25day coarse cases. `hlle_cpu/flux_checks.cpp` checks both
superfast upwind branches, three-vector rotation and the exact normal GLM flux.
`hlle_cpu/verify_brio.py` compares400/800/1600 first-order tube profiles with the
frozen independent Athena++8192 numerical branch; Brio–Wu is not claimed to have
a unique exact branch.

`mhd_cuda_hlle_reference` is a separate float64 implementation check. It supports
the optional electric correction and outer scaling, and deliberately rejects
nonempty cone input. Full coarse CPU/GPU snapshot arrays, probe bytes and
timestep/retry/divergence statistics match exactly. FP32 versus float64 on that
test changes PN incident flux by at most0.0357% pointwise, while local transverse
magnetic-field snapshot differences reach3.95% of the field maximum; these are
distinct precision diagnostics. The latter should not be hidden by the good
probe agreement.

The `*_async` variants batch stage failure flags on the device. A persistent
flag causes every dependent ghost/flux/RHS/update kernel to return; the host
then restores the conserved backup before retrying or writing probes. The
reconstruction, physical flux and RK arithmetic are unchanged. Full coarse
global/split/CME comparisons and a short wide96 case require identical snapshot
arrays, probe bytes and retry/diagnostic statistics in `validate_async.py`.

`mhd_cuda_fp32_async_hlld` is a separate contact/Alfvén-resolving control using
`flux_variant=split_hlld`. The shared float/double `hlld_kernel.hpp` implements
the five-wave construction of Miyoshi and Kusano(2005),
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcp.2005.02.017, with coordinate-free tangential vectors.
Formula/degeneracy review used the official Athena++ implementation; its source
attribution and BSD license are preserved in HLLD_ATTRIBUTION.txt and
HLLD_ATHENA_BSD_LICENSE.txt. The common interface q²/2 is excluded from every MHD
star energy; the common GLM energy flux ch*q*Bn is added afterward, with exact
normal-B/q fluxes. No cleaning energy is advected with the MHD velocity.

Near-degenerate denominators(relative tolerance1e-6), nonpositive density or gas
pressure in either star family, inconsistent wave ordering, or nonfinite flux
select the local HLLE flux. Nothing is clipped. `hlld_fallbacks.json` counts each
reason and every interface evaluation, including rejected RK attempts. A zero
normal field retains the contact-resolving hydrodynamic limit when regular.
`step_histogram.csv` records accepted steps, global first-order fallback steps and
rejected attempts by the integer UTC day at step start. Those are separate from
the interface HLLE fallbacks.

`build_hlld.py`, `validate_hlld.py`, `hlld_cpu/flux_checks.cpp`,
`hlld_cpu/glm_energy_check.cpp` and `hlld_cpu/verify_brio.py` reproduce the checks.
The64-bit CUDA reference rejects nonempty cone input; the32-bit production
control retains the cone and E interfaces. Complete25day CPU/CUDA64 coarse runs
have identical snapshot arrays, probe bytes, timestep/retry/divB statistics,
interface counters and daily histograms. FP32 maximum PN incident-flux precision
difference is0.400%(mean0.184%); local transverse-velocity and magnetic snapshot
differences are larger. This meets the1% proton-flux gate, not the original0.1%
precision target, and does not establish mesh or input convergence.
3I/ATLAS solar-wind MHD reconstruction — Codex

STATUS: provisional research reconstruction. Full numerical convergence is
not established. Passing a fixed-method refinement test does not resolve the
observed numerical-method sensitivity. See the prominent report warning.

Open report.html for the scientific results, assumptions and validation.
figures/comet_timeseries.png contains the three requested time-series charts.
figures/solar_wind_topdown.mp4 is the simulated inner-solar-system animation.
results/comet_timeseries.csv preserves heliocentric and comet-frame quantities.

All source, copied observations, provenance, derived products and monitoring
records are inside this directory. External Python packages and the C++/ffmpeg
toolchains are the only dependencies. Existing analysis and manuscripts are
read-only sources; regenerating the final simulation uses the copied inputs.

Reproduction from this directory, with Python 3.12 and the packages listed in
requirements.txt, GCC with OpenMP, GNU time and ffmpeg installed:

    make all

Existing completed simulations are reused. To rerun all production and control
simulations as well as regenerate the products, use `make all FORCE=--force`.
The wider fine run has 1200 s wall / 2400 s CPU caps; normal runs use the
900 s wall / 1800 s CPU caps below. These remain per-run hard limits.

No network access is needed for this reproduction. Acquisition scripts in
observations/ and external_model/ document retrieval from NASA, NSO and JPL;
refreshing the upstream archives is separate from reproducing the frozen run.
The solver is C++17, OpenMP with at most two threads per run. The Python runner
uses nice +15, a 1536 MB address-space cap, an 1800 s CPU-time cap and a 900 s
wall-time cap, terminating the entire process group on timeout. Solver arrays
have their own 700 MB guard. Production runs and parameter controls are small;
each run records its actual grid (including the medium frozen-field controls).
Final reports
state numerical limitations and do not equate convergence with accuracy.

Folders:
  inputs/         rotating WSA maps, probe tracks and calibration metadata
  observations/   local manuscript/spacecraft/GTI/Horizons extraction and evidence
  external_model/ actual CCMC output, WSA/GONG and coronagraph source provenance
  solver/         C++ solver, analytic/literature tests and divergence audit
  results/        individual run configurations, probe data, outputs and timing
  figures/        scientific plots, animation and preview
  validation/     criteria registered before reviewing refinement, native checks
  monitoring/     runtime, process/memory samples, token snapshots and progress

Shared timestamped collaboration notes live in ../shared_notes as requested.
They identify Codex-root and each Codex sub-agent separately. Token counts in
monitoring/ are the tool-reported goal counters, not a provider billing audit.
"}

Pre-epoch STEREO-A and Solar Orbiter measurements over November 10–24 set instrument-balanced density, magnetic and thermal normalizations. Wind is entirely held out. The calibrated boundary uses n₄₀₀={f(m["density_1au_at400_cm3"])} cm⁻³ at 1 AU, T₄₀₀={f(m["proton_temperature_01au_at400_K"])} K at the inner boundary, and a WSA field multiplier {f(m["WSA_Br_multiplier"])}. At native map nodes, constant momentum flux sets n∝v⁻² and constant thermal pressure sets T∝v². Independent linear interpolation of these primitive fields does not exactly preserve those nonlinear relations between nodes; that boundary-interpolation assumption is audited separately. Pressure is 2nₚkBTₚ, assuming equal electron and proton temperatures and hydrogen-only mass density. The chosen WSA-to-MHD speed reduction is 50 km/s; it is tested as an uncertain model choice, not represented as the exact ENLIL boundary transformation.

', + '

The thermodynamic interpolation audit samples the actual boundary, rather than assuming constant pressure between map nodes. Separate linear interpolation raises sampled source-band pressure by a median 0.99%, a 99th percentile 28.8%, and up to 75.7% on the combined spatial/time grid. Native-spatial-node hourly samples reach a factor 2.014; these are sampled maxima rather than analytic upper bounds. A separate optional closure interpolates speed first, then computes n=C/v² and T=Dv², with scalar normalization factors and conditional CME changes applied afterward. Its default-off control reproduces the original; 8000 CPU queries verify the enabled algebra. The new closure is a different controlled driver and must not be conflated with historical primitive-interpolated runs. Sampling details and equations; CPU control and provenance.

', + '

The nominal calibrated boundary is super-fast in the radial characteristic audit: the sampled actual-map minimum is about 1.21, and a conservative bound over positive interpolation weights is 1.048. This supports prescribing all nominal inner-boundary variables. It is not a general result for arbitrary field/density rescaling; the parameter audit explicitly records the margin to criticality. Optional inductive corrections were checked separately. Fast-wave equations, domain, sampling and bounds.
